q: How do I estimate the carbon footprint of a lathe or CNC machine I export?
title: Lathe or CNC machine footprint per unit
short: Add the castings and steel by mass times their factors, the bought-in motors, drives, controller and other parts from supplier figures or by mass, and your assembly and test energy per machine. For most machine tools the castings and bought-in electronics carry most of the cradle to gate footprint.
audience: Rajkot and Bengaluru machine tool makers

p: Beds, columns, saddles and tailstocks are usually grey or SG iron castings bought from a foundry. Use the foundry's figure per tonne of good casting if it has one, since a coke-fired cupola and an induction furnace give very different results. Add steel for spindles, guideways, sheet metal guards and fasteners, by mass bought.

ul: Spindle motor, servo motors and drives: supplier product figures if available, otherwise mass by material.
CNC controller and electronics: ask the supplier. Electronics are heavy in footprint for their weight, so a mass-only estimate tends to understate them; say how you estimated.
Ball screws, linear guides, bearings, hydraulics, coolant pump: supplier figures or mass by material.
Wooden crate and packing: by mass, if the buyer asks for packed product.

p: Machine tools are built in small numbers, so do not divide a month's power by machines shipped. Divide by assembly hours instead: each machine's share is its hours over total hours worked that month. Include machining of castings, painting, the test run and any accuracy checks.

sections.h: Use phase is a separate figure
p: A machine's electricity over its life usually dwarfs its manufacturing footprint. Buyers may ask how its energy use was evaluated under the ISO 14955 series: Part 1 covers design methodology for energy-efficient machine tools, and Part 2 covers measuring the energy a machine and its components take. Report that alongside the cradle to gate figure, not inside it.

example.title: Illustrative example: a 3 tonne CNC lathe
lines: Steel parts 600 kg x 2.0 = 1,200 kg CO2e
Motors and drives 120 kg x 5.0 = 600 kg CO2e
Controller and electronics: supplier figure 400 kg CO2e
Assembly: 400 of 4,000 shop hours in a 25,000 kWh month = 2,500 kWh, x 0.710 (FY 2024-25 grid factor) = 1,775 kg CO2
Total: 3,000 + 1,200 + 600 + 400 + 1,775 = 6,975 kg CO2e, about 7.0 tonnes per machine
example.note: Material factors (kg CO2e per kg) and the controller figure are placeholders to show the arithmetic. Use your foundry's, steel mill's and suppliers' own figures.

senseible: Senseible reads your workshop's electricity and fuel bills into Scope 1 and 2 totals, which you share across machines by assembly hours. Casting and component factors come from your suppliers or published data.
